issues.description: The SAS source compares CIK with company_fkey using ordinary equality; the frozen catalog types show Compustat CIK as Char(11) and Audit Analytics company_fkey as Char(10). No conversion/padding/crosswalk is supplied, so verify that the local extracts’ key representation is compatible with the authored equality. The code explicitly uses the prior-year ICW match and an intnx('year',datadate,-1) restatement interval; preserve those written timing rules while checking the raw dates/identifiers.

No author-prepared analysis dataset is supplied. Six local catalog candidates for the documented Compustat and Audit Analytics products are readable in row_limit=1 probes, but those probes do not verify the full issuer population, required years, source vintage or construction compatibility. The US 2004–2013 subgroup branch requires three earlier same-month accounting years (at least 2001–2013); Global 2013 outputs require three prior years (at least 2010–2013); the Audit Analytics date coverage must align with the actual prior-year match and interval joins. Company fields are joined from company/g_company before later keep statements.

README Step 3 lists the Table5 and Table8A country/subgroup MAT destinations in reverse order from actual driver loads. Actual Table5 drivers consume four compicw01 subgroup matrices; Table8A, like Table3467/Table8B5/Table8B10, consumes country 2013 matrices. Appendix 2 supplies the MATLAB7 transfer settings and a compc2013 example; SAS output names and driver loads define the other six files. The remaining contract to verify is the produced st_dataset field/type mapping and runtime compatibility, while every folder-relative load/export path must be preserved.

The README specifies SAS 9.4, MATLAB R2017a, StatTransfer 13 and Knitro 12.2.1. The bounded SAS startup attempt fails at TKELS with return code 1; MATLAB, StatTransfer and Knitro are not discoverable on PATH. Availability of simulannealbnd, knitromatlab, chi2cdf, xlswrite, required toolbox/interface components, licenses and the workbook calculation engine remains unverified. These observations are not evidence of missing licenses; no author routine or optimizer was run.

Table2.xlsx and Figure4.xlsx contain supplied formula programs for the README manual paste workflow, but the calculation engine/version and exact paste ranges are unspecified. Static inspection counted 126 and 210 formulas, respectively, without evaluating formulas or cached values. README calls Figure4 files sensitivity_f4, while the country drivers emit sensitibity_f4; use the exact native output names and confirm the input ranges in the supported spreadsheet engine.

evidence.description: README names six WRDS source datasets and the Compustat and Audit Analytics download route.
evidence.quote:
Using WRDS, users can download four files from Compustat and two files from Audit Analytics. The
following four files can be downloaded from Compustat: funda, g_funda, company, and g_company. Users
can use the code in Appendix 1 to download these files. The following two files can be downloaded directly
from WRDS / Audit Analytics: icwrestatement (SOX 404 Internal Controls) and aa_res (Restatements).
icwrestatement and aa_res are just the names used in the included SAS code (ConstructData). The specific
sections of Audit Analytics to download these datasets are described in the parentheses. Users can download
the full datasets in each section of Audit Analytics on WRDS and name them as “icwretatement” and
“aa_res”, respectively for the data processing purpose.

actions.description: Check that the local Compustat and Audit Analytics extracts use compatible CIK/company_fkey values and dates for the exact prior-year joins already written in ConstructData.sas.
steps: Compare CIK Char(11) and company_fkey Char(10) using the raw source definitions and actual local values; report whether the source values match under the existing equality without guessing, padding, truncating or recoding.
Check the raw IC opinion dates against the exact authored `year-1` match and the restatement begin/end dates against the exact `intnx('year',datadate,-1)` interval.
Preserve both SAS join expressions and sample timing as written; treat incompatibility, if found, as unresolved pending evidence rather than changing the model definition.
validation: During a later authorized data validation, report key-match coverage and type conversion behavior without changing author definitions.

actions.description: Validate the six readable local catalog candidates against the author-defined Compustat and Audit Analytics source products, period coverage, population and company identifiers; if they are not the compatible complete inputs, acquire those exact products through the documented WRDS route.
steps: For each existing local candidate, confirm it is the intended source product and complete source vintage; each current bounded read sampled one row and verified no historical/population coverage.

Retain the source filters: North America consol=C, indfmt=INDL, datafmt=STD, popsrc=D; Global consol=C, indfmt=INDL, datafmt=HIST_STD, popsrc=I, with the author’s India IND/INR and China CHN/CNY country/currency selections.
Keep the author’s gvkey join from funda/g_funda to company/g_company before later keep statements; do not invent aliases for company fields or edit the source.

Verify at least 2001–2013 North America annual history for the 2004–2013 ICW/restatement branch and at least 2010–2013 Global history for the 2013 country files; confirm any wider author source ranges from the actual full extracts.
Confirm Audit Analytics field formats, full required date coverage, CIK/company_fkey representation, the prior-year ICW match, and the restatement date intervals before accepting local compatibility.
validation: Check exact source product, required fields/types and complete population/date coverage after acquisition; one-row probes alone do not prove them.
Verify author-prescribed source filters, joins and generated row coverage without recoding timing or identifiers based on guessed conventions.

actions.description: Run the documented SAS → StatTransfer 13 MATLAB7 → per-folder MATLAB workflow using actual producer/consumer paths, while preserving each country and ICW/restatement branch and every helper file.
steps: Copy the six source products from their distinct source roots into a separate staged working Data folder; set Folder to that project root so CAL reads the staged inputs and writes derived datasets beside them without writing back to the source roots.

Use the documented Appendix 2 MATLAB7 settings and repeat its SAS7BDAT-to-MAT conversion for each exact named output: compc2013, compgchnc2013, compgindc2013, compicw01res, compicw01nres, compicw01ie and compicw01e. The SAS outputs and MATLAB driver loads identify the other six targets; no additional scientific transformation is implied.

Copy the three country 2013 MAT files into Table3467, Table8A, Table8B5 and Table8B10, where the actual country drivers load them; copy the four ICW/restatement subgroup MAT files into Table5, where its drivers load them. This corrects the reversed Table5/Table8A destination wording in README Step 3 using the actual driver inputs.

Before any model run, verify each MAT produces the author-used st_dataset with acl1, acl2, ael1, ael2, acgl1, aegl1, investg and industry2, preserving column types and row order as expected by the source.

Run only the 16 supplied SMMEstimation_*.m drivers, each with its own estimate_model subfolder as current folder; retain all 51 same-folder helper .m files as called-function closure. Do not treat criterionFunction, policyFunction or other stateful helper files as standalone launches.

Preserve original dimensions, random seeds, sample branches, multi values, SMM moments, simulated-annealing initialization, Knitro refinement and branch-specific policy functions; do not substitute a different estimator or collapse Table8B5 and Table8B10.
validation: Verify each SAS producer, StatTransfer MAT and MATLAB relative load matches the exact table-country/subgroup handoff mapped in workflow_trace.json.
Check the eight expected st_dataset fields and downstream MATLAB output names after an authorized run; do not run estimators as a feasibility check.

actions.description: Resolve runtime availability and exact function/interface/license capability for the author-specified software through bounded metadata checks, without running estimation or simulation.
steps: Verify SAS 9.4 startup/configuration after reviewing the TKELS diagnostic; the current status is unverified and does not establish license availability.

When MATLAB R2017a is locatable, use only non-estimator metadata queries to confirm the exact `simulannealbnd`, `knitromatlab`, `chi2cdf` and `xlswrite` resolutions, associated required toolbox/interface components and license capability; do not invoke any optimizer or model function.
Verify StatTransfer 13 and its MATLAB7 writer path, and verify Knitro 12.2.1 MATLAB interface/license through supported software metadata.
Identify an available spreadsheet engine/version and check its formula/workbook support using software metadata only; keep formula evaluation for a separately authorized reproduction run.
validation: Record software release, exact function resolution, required feature/license checks and command/process diagnostics in JSON under this package's probes directory.
Do not install packages or execute author code, estimator/optimizer functions, synthetic trials, or workbook recalculation as part of a metadata check.

actions.description: Preserve the supplied Table2 and Figure4 formula programs, document their manual inputs, and establish the supported workbook engine/version and exact paste ranges.
steps: Use the original Table2.xlsx (SHA256 f60940212306e40529aa474fbc0c904c0be310778e22c5cdf145939a50692912) and Figure4.xlsx (SHA256 bb6206d1a06fc70cb40e001d4d1b6322f4c980083c8967d7e3111e5cba6367ef) as the workbook-program entry points; preserve all formula bytes and existing sheet/cell structure.
For Table2, paste t2_dsus, t2_dschina and t2_dsindia into the documented yellow areas on dsus, dschn and dsind; the table sheet contains the supplied formula program.
For Figure3, paste the Table3467 US simulation_f3 output into the supplied Figure3 template; it has no inspected formula/pivot program.

For Figure4, the README says sensitivity_f4_US/China/India, while the drivers write sensitibity_f4_US/China/India.xlsx; locate the actual source-produced filenames and confirm the matching yellow country ranges in the supported spreadsheet engine.

Identify an available spreadsheet engine/version and confirm it supports the stored workbook formulas and required manual paste operation. Do not use Office/LibreOffice, recalculate, refresh pivots or dereference external links during this static feasibility assessment.
validation: In a later authorized execution using the supported engine, confirm workbook sheets, manual input ranges and resulting formula cells after outputs exist.
Retain the frozen workbook hashes and do not patch binary XLSX files or substitute cached values.

review_notes: Full source review is complete for all 75 frozen source entries (5,335 code lines, 1,447 document lines and 4 data/template lines); 43 unique source hashes are represented. Workflow trace records all 16 estimation drivers, 51 required same-folder helper files, all 37 dependency IDs, workbook programs and one-row raw-source probe results.

Only actual drivers, ConstructData.sas and original formula-bearing Table2/Figure4 workbooks are entry points. MATLAB helpers remain in closure and are called with driver state. All source outputs, country/subgroup branches, native sample/definitions, SMM/optimizer sequence and workbook formulas remain preserved.

Six local SAS catalog source candidates passed row_limit=1 readability/field probes, but population and date coverage remain unverified. Company fields used after keep are supplied by the joined company tables; CIK/company_fkey type-length and timing semantics remain unresolved.

Workbook inspection was static XML only. No author SAS/MATLAB/StatTransfer/Knitro code, estimator, optimizer, simulation, workbook formula, pivot or cached value was executed or recalculated; no source or model changes are proposed.

No analysis_only scope is supported: the packaged CompanyIdentifiers workbook contains a GVKEY identifier list, while the result workbooks are templates and the full workflow requires the six separate raw source products.
